summary: Missing mid-cycle prorated credit for Dedicated committed-hours — hourly metering not reflecting credit
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that a custom reserved commitment purchased mid-billing-cycle applied as a prorated credit at purchase time, but subsequent hourly metering continued to bill against raw usage without the committed-hour credit being applied.

Impact: ParcelLogic is seeing an unexpected spike in invoices for the current month estimated at ~$9k above expected after they purchased a 2k-hour dedicated commitment on 2026-03-05. They are mid-market, production workloads, reporting degraded confidence in billing accuracy.

Environment: Production (dedicated), us-east-1. Commitment purchased via Console by customer billing admin on 2026-03-05.

Steps to reproduce / provided by customer:
1) On 2026-03-05 customer purchased a 2000-hour dedicated commitment (custom pricing) with immediate prorated application for remainder of billing cycle.
2) Console shows a credit line applied on 2026-03-05 for prorated commitment value.
3) Hourly invoices and metering records for hours after 2026-03-05 still show full on-demand rates in metering exports and in the daily invoice preview for 2026-03-06 to 2026-03-11.
4) Customer cross-checked token-level metering CSV and found usage tagged to the org/project but not tagged as "commit-applied" in the metering exports.

Expected behavior: Metering and hourly billing should decrement usable committed-hours first (or show a matching credit line allocation) so invoice reflects lower effective unit cost for hours within the prorated commitment.

Actual behavior: Console credit exists but hourly metering and invoice preview do not offset usage. Customer attachments: screenshots of Console credit entry, CSV of daily metering export (redacted), and invoice preview PDF.

Notes: Customer explicitly used a custom commit (not a standard plan). They are subscribed to Dedicated with reserved GPU pool. They indicated this behavior has not happened on prior commitments purchased earlier in their contract period.
steps_to_reproduce: Purchase custom dedicated-hour commitment mid-cycle via Console
Verify that a prorated credit line appears in Billing -> Credits
Run daily metering export for usage rows after purchase
Observe that usage rows do not include commit-allocation tag and invoice preview shows on-demand rates
logs_and_evidence: API audit log: billing.create_commitment id=commit_8721 by user=alice@parcellogic.com 2026-03-05T14:08:32Z
customer_communication_summary: 2026-03-10 09:12 PDT - Customer reported via support form: 'We paid for a mid-cycle commitment but still being billed full hourly rates. Need immediate review.'
2026-03-10 10:05 PDT - Support (Nina): requested metering export and invoice preview; asked for commit purchase confirmation (attached).
2026-03-11 15:30 PDT - Customer follow-up: provided redacted CSV showing usage rows lacking commit tag; says finance needs a hold on next invoice until resolved.
investigation_notes: 03-10 11:00 - Initial triage: confirmed credit line exists in billing ledger for org_id=org_4102 dated 2026-03-05.
03-10 13:20 - Pulled metering export for org_4102 2026-03-06..2026-03-11: usage rows present, all tagged 'billing_tier:on_demand' and missing 'billing_tier:commit' tag used by proration allocator.

03-10 16:45 - Checked commitment service logs: commit_8721 created and scheduled for allocation job 'commit-allocator-v2'. Allocation job shows success event but with warning: 'allocation: partial-match: tag-mismatch for resource_group=dedicated-pool-32'.

03-11 09:10 - Hypothesis: commit-allocator failed to match usage rows because customer uses a custom resource_group label on dedicated pool that the allocator does not canonicalize. Possible bug introduced in allocator canonicalization PR merged 2026-02-28.

03-11 12:00 - Reproduced in staging: create custom-named dedicated pool, buy mid-cycle commit; allocation job succeeds but metering export lacks 'commit' tag when pool name contains an uppercase character or unusual separator. Failing string normalization path in allocation logic confirmed.

03-11 14:40 - Scoped blast radius: affects custom commitments created mid-cycle for dedicated pools with non-canonical names. Does not affect legacy standard-plan commits created via sales onboarding flow.

03-11 17:20 - Quick mitigation: manual reconcile by applying commit allocation to metering rows for affected orgs and regenerating invoice preview. Long-term fix requires allocator normalization patch and additional test coverage.
customer_priority_impact: Finance hold requested by customer until correction applied
Estimated invoice delta: ~$9,000 overstated for current month
Customer relationship: risk of escalation to account management if not resolved within 72 hours
action_items: Apply manual reconciliation credits to org_4102 metering rows for 2026-03-06..2026-03-11 (billing team)
Backport allocator canonicalization fix to production (engineering)
Add end-to-end test covering pool-name variations for commit allocation (QA)
Notify customer when manual reconcile and production patch deployed (Support/CS)
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Nina Patel (Support): Thanks for the details — we've received the metering CSV and invoice preview. We're escalating to billing and engineering to triage the allocation flow.
2026-03-11 12:30 - Diego Ramos (Billing): I pulled the allocation job logs; there's an apparent mismatch between pool identifier formats. I'll queue a manual reconcile while engineering investigates.

2026-03-11 18:05 - Mateo Alvarez (SRE): Confirmed reproducer in staging. Allocator fails normalization when pool names include uppercase characters or dashes combined with underscore. Preparing a patch PR.

2026-03-12 09:10 - Nina Patel (Support) -> ParcelLogic billing admin (Alice Chang): We will apply a provisional credit for the overstated amount and hold the invoice. Engineering aims to deploy a fix within 48 hours; billing will follow up with a reconciliation report.
2026-03-12 15:50 - Alice Chang (ParcelLogic): Acknowledged and appreciates the quick response; requested a ledger entry that documents the provisional credit for their internal auditors.
resolution: Provisional steps performed: billing applied manual reconciliation credits to org_4102 for the affected date range and generated a corrected invoice preview; customer invoice placed on administrative hold pending final patch. Engineering merged allocator canonicalization fix (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/548) and scheduled canary rollout to prod. QA added regression tests for pool name variations. Final resolution pending successful canary; customer will be notified and final invoice adjusted if canary confirms fix.
final_status_notes: Pending canary rollout as of 2026-03-12. Manual reconcile applied and customer notified. Recommend closure after prod verification and customer acceptance.
